endorsements.quote: Possible additional checks by other LLMs, or assigning the role of ‘checker’ to an agent-based LLM

If cybersecurity expertise or access to the right equipment (either physically or through cloud-based solutions) is not available to the analyst, it is highly recommended to avoid working with confidential data.

For example, it can be contractually agreed that data sent to the LLM will not be used to train future model iterations, a significant concern for businesses using proprietary or commercially sensitive data.

Techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can help mitigate this by enabling the model to retrieve factual information from external sources, such as policy documents or clinical guidelines, before generating a response [ 55 ].

unlisted_practices: Always keep a human in the loop for AI-assisted HEOR work, with final decision-making remaining with humans.
Declare the exact LLM version and date used in any HEOR work.
Describe the prompting techniques and contextual information used to generate LLM content.
Compare LLM process output with a human gold-standard benchmark on a subset of the problem at first use.
Validate LLM-generated code for economic models or network meta-analyses as rigorously as human-written code.
Do not use LLM architecture and weights directly to run network meta-analyses or cost-effectiveness analyses.
Use low temperature, fixed seeds, and self-consistency approaches to improve LLM reproducibility.
Break complex questions into smaller tasks (task decomposition) and use one API call per task.
Use API access rather than chatbot interfaces for complex or large-scale HEOR projects.
Use sandboxed environments for LLMs to mitigate prompt injection.
Forecast likely usage and costs before opting for hosted LLM APIs.
Assess each use case to determine the level of ethical scrutiny and transparency required.
Use pre-emptive testing and benchmarking to detect LLM bias.
